items.title: Trump suggests new talks with Iran to begin on Monday
items.description: Tehran has not responded to the suggestion that new talks are imminent. Trump has previously said a negotiated end to the war is close, only for strikes to resume.

items.title: 'My only son was shot standing up for justice' - inside city gripped by deadly protests in Pakistan-administered Kashmir
items.description: The BBC gains unique access to Rawalakot, scene of violent clashes between security forces and protesters in Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

items.title: Aung San Suu Kyi appears healthy in first confirmed outside contact for 2.5 years
items.description: Photos newly released by Myanmar's military government show Suu Kyi meeting with an ICRC official.

items.title: US and Japan take action to prop up yen in rare joint move
items.description: Both countries have said that they will not hesitate to conduct joint interventions in the future.

items.title: Two crew killed after firefighting helicopters collide in Greece, as British pilot survives
items.description: One Danish and one Greek national died in the incident, while a British pilot and another Greek crew member survived.

items.title: Ariana Grande to take a break from public life amid 'endless' scrutiny
items.description: The US singer, 33, will "step back from visibility" at the end of her world tour next month, her representative says.

items.title: Malaysian boy on trial for allegedly murdering girl in school
items.description: The high-profile case has shocked Malaysia and sparked debate about the effect of social media on children.

items.title: 'Your legacy will live forever': Nepal mourns climber Nirmal Purja
items.description: Tributes are pouring out across Nepal after an avalanche killed some of the country's best mountaineers.

items.title: Massive Attack respond after Singapore ban over Palestine display
items.description: The UK band says they are "surprised and disappointed" by their treatment over shouting "free Palestine" at a concert there.

items.title: Outside the Moscow restaurant where bomb killed three
items.description: The BBC's Russia editor reports from Kudrinskaya Square, where the blast took place.

items.title: At least 13 killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza after Hamas agree disarmament deal
items.description: Israel says it was targeting military operatives in the strikes on Gaza City, Khan Younis and Deir el-Balah.

items.title: Uganda unveils statue of Israel PM's brother who died in Entebbe rescue mission
items.description: Yonatan Netanyahu was the only Israeli soldier to die as he led a mission to free more than 100 hostages.

items.title: Tourist plane crashes in Peru, killing 13
items.description: The small plane was flying over the Nazca Lines ​archaeological site when it crashed, according to local reports.

items.title: Italy putting nearly all major cities on highest heat alert
items.description: Some 19 major Italian cities - including Rome, Milan and Naples - are already on red alert, and by Monday all but two will be.

items.title: Three killed after bomb detonated at Moscow restaurant, state media say
items.description: Security officials said a woman tried to enter the restaurant with explosives but was stopped by a security guard.

items.title: Body of mountaineer Nirmal Purja recovered after Pakistan avalanche
items.description: The renowned climber was known for scaling the world's 14 highest peaks in just over six months in 2019.

items.title: 'What was my fault?': How India's exam paper leak ended young lives
items.description: Two families reveal the human toll of India's medical entrance examination paper leak.

items.title: A bruising 24 hours - what next for Fifa and under-pressure Infantino?
items.description: Pressure is building on Gianni Infantino. Can he survive as Fifa president after the implosion of the controversial World Cup investment plan?

items.title: How Spain's migrant crisis created a political storm - whipped up by social media
items.description: The Ceuta crossings have shaken Europe politically, exposing divisions over the sensitive issue of migration, the BBC's Sarah Rainsford writes.

items.title: How Australia combines modern tech and Indigenous knowledge to fight wildfires
items.description: As Europe faces its worst wildfires in decades, Australia offers lessons in disaster preparedness.
